chunks: From him, from al-Naḍr, from Muḥammad ibn Abī Ḥamzah, from Muʿāwiyah ibn ʿAmmār, who said:
I said to Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام: “The taslīm in the two rakʿahs of al-watr?” He said: “If you wish, you may say the taslīm, and if you wish, you may refrain from saying the taslīm.”

key_terms.التَّسْلِيمُ: the concluding salutation ending a salat (prayer)
key_terms.الْوَتْرِ: the witr prayer in the night prayer context

ai.seo_question: Is saying the taslīm in the two rakʿahs of al-watr obligatory or optional?
ai.summary: This hadith addresses the ruling of saying the taslīm in the two rakʿahs associated with al-watr prayer. Imam al-Ṣādiq عليه السلام states that it is optional, indicating permissibility rather than obligation in this specific act of worship.
